descript.abstract: These data are associated with the work described in NPRB Final Report R0314 (http://doc.nprb.org/web/03_prjs/r0314_final.pdf) and in Loher, 2008 (Deep Sea Research II, 55(16-17):1801-1808). During the summers of 2003 (June 12 through September 12) and 2004 (June 2 through September 26), two varieties of temperarature recorders were deployed at St. Paul Island, Alaska, from a total of 13 local commercial longline vessels during normal fishing operations, generally conducted within five nautical miles of the Island's coastline. During 2003, TSKA WaDaR temperature recorders (TSKA, North Bend, Washington, USA) were deployed from six vessels; loggers were programmed to record temperature at 5 minute intervals, temperature-dependent resolutions ranging from 0.0011 C to 0.0014 C at minimum and maximum temperature, respectively, and better than + 0.05 C. Vemco Minilog temperature-depth recorders (Vemco, Shad Bay, Nova Scotia, Canada) were deployed from twelve vessels in 2003 and 2004; loggers were programmed to record temperature and depth at either four or five minute intervals with temperature at 0.1 C resolution and 0.2 C accuracy, and pressures equivalent to 0-800 m of seawater at 3.6 m resolution and 15 m accuracy. Raw data were output as comma-delimited text files with temperature-depth readings referenced to date and time. The deployments provide data from 266 longline sets in 2003 and 351 sets in 2004. These datasets were archived as part of the North Pacific Research Board legacy project recovery effort undertaken by Axiom Data Science and NPRB in 2025. The goal of the recovery effort was to assess the NPRB-funded data projects from 2002 to 2014 and archive final data packages that were ready for publication to increase long-term accessibility and discoverability. Data packages were archived as is given limited funding and resources.
descript.purpose: The study was conducted to characterize the annual shallow-water warming trend and test the hypothesis that commercial CPUE in the local fishery varies on intra-annual (weeks to months) and inter-annual (among fishing seasons) time scales. The latter was accomplished by correlating vessel-standardized set temperatures to catch and effort data retrieved from confidential vessel logbook and IPHC landings data.

attracc.attraccr: WaDaRs recorded temperatures between -3 to 30C at temperature-dependent resolutions ranging from 0.0011 degree at -3 C to 0.0014 degree at 30 C, with better than + 0.05 degree accuracy at all temperatures. Units were not new at the beginning of the project, but were sent to the manufacturer in 2002 for calibration and logging of internal calibration coefficients, as recommended on a bienniel basis. Calibrations were conducted in controlled water baths at Scripps Institute of Oceanography, San Diego, CA. Vemco Minilogs recorded temperatures between -4 C and 20 C at 0.1 degree resolution and 0.2 degree accuracy, and pressures equivalent to 0-800 m of seawater at 3.6 m resolution and 15 m accuracy. These values were certified by the manufacturer and all units were new at the beginning of the 2003 field season. Units were not recalibrated prior to 2004.

dataqual.logic: All data files contain contiguous data from the shipping date prior to deployment until after the loggers had been retrieved from the fishers. Errant values are possible, and have not been removed from the data set; individual investigators should use their own judgement when screening data for outliers.
dataqual.complete:
WaDaRs do not record depth. Therefore, in-water deployements must be inferred from stability of the temperature reading (which is more stable when the logger is in water than when it is in air), cross-referenced to fisher logbook data that provides time-of-set data for commercial longline sets. Because the latter are proprietary and cannot be included in the publically-accessable data, this data set lists times of set and retrieval for each WaDaR, as verified by logbook data.
*** NOTE that catch and effort data are not included here. These are proprietary and cannot be released publicly. Requests for such data in summarized form may be made by contacting the IPHC Fisheries Statistics Program Managear (Heather Gilroy) at 206-634-1838 ext 206, or via email at heather@iphc.washington.edu. ***
*** NOTE that in all cases, data in the files is contiguous and has not been screened to eliminate periods of non-deployment (logger not in the sea) from periods of deployment (logger in the sea). ***

overview.eaover: The available data set contains data in three forms: *** 1. WaDaR data - Eight comma-delimited text files where the first value in each line is time of day (UTC-10), the second value is temperature (Celsius), and the third is the calendar date. The file name is prefixed with "wadar", followed by the 3-digit logger number, followed by the year of deployment. *** 2. "wadarDeployLog.xls" - This Excel file lists times of set and retrieval for each WaDaR, as verified by logbook data. *** 3. Minilog data - Twenty six comma-delimited text files that begin with a header section identifying the logger and detailing deployment information, followed by the data-region wherein the first value is the calendar date (note that these are in day-month-year format), the second is time of day (UTC-10), the third is temperature (Celsius), and the fourth is water depth (m). The file name is prefixed with "minilog", followed by the 4-digit logger number, followed by the year of deployment; where a logger was downloaded mid-season, the file representing the first half of the season ends in "a" and the file representing the second half ends in "b".
